questions.prompt: What did the Bracero Program, agreed between Mexico and the United States in 1942, arrange?
options: Contracts for Mexican men to work on US farms
Duty-free assembly plants along the border
The return of the Chamizal tract to Mexico
Free trade among Mexico, the US and Canada
questions.explanation: Begun because the United States was at war and short of farm labour, the program issued some 4.6 million contracts before the US Congress let it lapse at the end of 1964. With the program ended and unemployment high along the border, Mexico launched the maquiladora program in 1965.

questions.prompt: Two weeks after soldiers and police fired on protesters in León's main square in January 1946, the official party was refounded under what name?
questions.explanation: The Unión Cívica Leonesa had claimed victory in the municipal election of December 1945; officially 36 people were killed in the square, and the Senate removed Guanajuato's governor, Ernesto Hidalgo. The official party, founded in 1929, now took the name Partido Revolucionario Institucional.

questions.prompt: Acapulco was turned into Mexico's first great beach resort in the 1940s and 1950s. Where is Acapulco? Click the map.
questions.explanation: Miguel Alemán, as interior minister and then president, promoted the expropriation of beachfront land for hotels and the coastal road named after him, and migrants who came to work in the hotels settled in the hills behind the bay. From the 1970s federal investment shifted to Cancún.

questions.prompt: Ciudad Juárez, across from El Paso, became the largest centre of the Border Industrialization Program launched in 1965. Where is Ciudad Juárez? Click the map.
questions.explanation: The program let foreign-owned assembly plants (maquiladoras) import parts and machinery duty-free as long as they exported the product. Juárez's industrial parks of US electronics, garment and auto-parts plants employed mostly young women.

questions.prompt: The massacre at Tlatelolco on 2 October 1968 came ten days before which event?
options: The opening of the Olympic Games
The army's occupation of Ciudad Universitaria
The bazooka attack on San Ildefonso
questions.explanation: Soldiers and the plain-clothes Olimpia Battalion opened fire on a student rally in the Plaza de las Tres Culturas. The government acknowledged a few dozen deaths; later estimates run from several dozen to more than 300, and the number has never been established.

questions.prompt: Operation Condor drove Sinaloan traffickers such as Félix Gallardo, Caro Quintero and Fonseca out of the sierra. In which city did they regroup as "the Federation"?
questions.explanation: With US money and DEA advisers, the army sent thousands of troops and herbicide-spraying aircraft into the Golden Triangle around Badiraguato, and peasant villages suffered torture, killings and displacement. The Guadalajara-based Federation ended after the 1985 murder of the DEA agent Enrique Camarena brought US pressure and the arrests of its leaders.

questions.prompt: Why did the earthquake of 19 September 1985 do far more damage in Mexico City than near its epicentre?
options: The soft clays of the old lake bed amplified the shaking
Its epicentre lay directly beneath the capital
It struck at night, when most people were asleep
Fire spread from the San Juanico gas terminal
questions.explanation: The magnitude 8.0 quake struck shortly after 7 a.m. off the coast of Michoacán, near Lázaro Cárdenas, nearly 400 km from the capital, and the coast close to the epicentre suffered relatively little. In Mexico City hundreds of buildings collapsed, and the government's slow response weakened the PRI's hold on the capital.

questions.prompt: Who ran against Carlos Salinas de Gortari at the head of a left-wing front in the disputed election of 1988?
questions.explanation: Cárdenas, son of the former president, broke with the PRI to run; on election night the Interior Ministry's counting system "crashed", and Salinas was then declared the winner with just over 50 per cent. The PRD, founded in 1989, grew out of Cárdenas's campaign.

questions.prompt: In 1989 the PRI conceded a governorship to the opposition for the first time since the party's founding. In which state?
questions.explanation: Ernesto Ruffo Appel of the PAN won on 2 July 1989, and the Salinas government recognised it. The opposition went on to win Chihuahua (1992), Guanajuato and Jalisco (1995) and Nuevo León (1997) before the PRI lost the presidency in 2000.

questions.prompt: In the first hours of 1 January 1994, as NAFTA took effect, the Zapatistas seized San Cristóbal de las Casas. Where is San Cristóbal? Click the map.
questions.explanation: From the balcony of the municipal palace the EZLN, mostly Maya from the highlands and the Lacandon forest, read its Declaration of the Lacandon Jungle, demanding land, work, health, education, democracy and justice. With the murders of Colosio and Ruiz Massieu later that year, the uprising made 1994 the year the PRI system visibly cracked.
